answer: Each identity registers one vertex, posting a 70-credit bond. Registration lists its inlet edges and a color, sealed with an umber seal binding vertex, color, and edges, published on the board. An auditor recomputes it: adjacent vertices must differ in color, and no inlet edge may be shared. The first registration costs 20 credits; the kth identity pays 20+5(k-1), so the 1000th pays 5015 and 1000 fakes pay 2,517,500 plus 70,000 locked. A color-copy ring fails: copied colors or shared edges mismatch and both burn. An honest operator pays 20 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
